pref_editor_snap_magnet_strength_desc: How strongly an existing onset pulls the note you are inserting, as a fraction of the slot. 0.5 = half a slot (stacking chords is easiest, breaking away for the next note is harder). 0 = magnet off, grid only.
pref_editor_avviso_incrocio_voci: Warn when an inserted note crosses voices
pref_editor_avviso_incrocio_voci_desc: Appears when inserting, not when opening a file: offers to swap the voices in one click.
pref_analysis_roman_bass_mode_hint: The Roman numeral shows the scale degree of the actual bass note (always uppercase); the chord is expressed by the figures. Requires “Show Roman numerals” on.
pref_analysis_enable_inferred_contexts_h: When enabled, the app may apply inferred key changes so Roman numerals such as V7 stay correct inside a modulation (e.g. an Eb/Cm section). It does not override manual contexts: explicit markers always win.
pref_analysis_statistical_correction_hin: Use statistics extracted from exercises to correct unlikely Roman labels. Requires a large exercise corpus.
pref_analysis_statistical_bias_threshold: R14 kicks in when the score difference between the two top candidates is below this threshold.
pref_analysis_learned_ornaments_hint: Automatically detect ornaments based on patterns learned from manual corrections.
pref_analysis_strict_passing_notes_hint: Apply tighter guards on the duration and ornamental profile of passing notes. Disable it to fall back to a more permissive behavior.
pref_analysis_tonicization_compact_hint: Show [in IV]: ii → V → I instead of ii/IV → V/IV → I/IV. Ideal for fast note values.
pref_analysis_cadential_patterns_hint: Automatically detect cadences (ii–V–I, IV–V–I, etc.) and inject temporary tonicizations toward the target key.
pref_analysis_chromatic_modulation_hint: Detect modulations without cadential preparation by analysing chromatic content over windows of ≥ 3 consecutive measures.
midi_output_hint: Choose where playback is sent: internal audio or an external MIDI device. This is the same setting as the toolbar menu.
pref_midi_export_type_description: Type 1 (multi-track): one track per voice — compatible with MuseScore/Finale/Sibelius. Type 0 (single track): all voices in one track — maximum compatibility.
analysis_profile_hint: A profile is a preset (it does not lock combinations). If you change toggles manually, the profile becomes "Custom".
analysis_profile_apply_preset_tooltip: Re-apply the base profile preset (restores defaults)
label_min_span_section_hint: Reduces clutter by sampling labels on a rhythmic grid (useful with sixteenths and double passing notes). It does not change the analysis: it is only a display filter.
label_min_span_select_label: Show labels only if they last at least:
rule_suggestions_hint: Customize the "Suggestion" text for each rule. Rule names and descriptions cannot be edited.
staff_line_weight_hint: The staff lines start from a light grey: here they can be darkened, and thickened a little. It helps on very dense screens and in print. The gain comes from contrast rather than thickness: a line that is too thick crowds the noteheads.
pref_editor_orchestral_grouping_desc: Draws a square bracket around consecutive staves of the same instrument family (woodwinds, brass, strings…), joins their barlines, and ties choir and tracks together with a single line on the left. The family is inferred from the track’s instrument and can be overridden by clicking the staff’s clef.
pref_editor_voice_from_chord_desc: Write notes without picking a voice: vertical order within the chord decides, the way a printed page reads — highest is soprano, lowest is bass. The order you write in does not matter, and neither does the staff (in close position the tenor sits on the treble staff). Rests keep the voice of wherever you place them, and say who is silent.
